feedback: No earlier race exists yet, so this feedback is prior-based and makes no claim about measured performance. Two things the Integrator had to set by hand from the contract alone: (1) the sensor weights had to be antisymmetric, [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], so a centred line gives a zero signal. This is only valid because the 12 mm footprints at 15 mm pitch leave the outer sensors blank when the robot is centred. (2) kp and kd had to be kept modest because the signal scale is set by the weights, which makes the steering gain sensitive to the sensor pitch. Once the Iteration 0 race reports, check the next result against these rules: if steering_oscillation is high or max_error is large on the S-bend, the sensor pitch or look-ahead is probably the cause. If line_loss_events are high only on the sharpest bends, the look-ahead of 0.04 m is too short. If the robot completes with low error, keep the 12 mm, 15 mm pitch layout and only adjust the track width.
requested_changes: If the next race shows line_loss_events on the sharpest bend and the robot leaves the line, move the sensors further ahead (y 0.05 to 0.06) to lengthen look-ahead, keeping x positions and sensor_size 0.012.

If the next race shows large steering_oscillation with low max_error, try sensor_size 0.016 with the same x positions to widen the sensor overlap and smooth the signal, since the 12 mm footprint is at the edge of resolving the 25 mm tape at 15 mm pitch.
If the robot tracks well but completion_time is above 3 s, try wheel_track 0.10 to increase turn authority and wheel_radius 0.035 to raise ground speed, without changing the sensor layout.
